problem.title: Existence of a biplanar graph with no proper nine-colouring
problem.informal_statement:
Decide whether there is a finite simple graph G whose edge set is the union of two planar graphs on the vertex set V(G) and whose chromatic number is at least 10.

Biplanar is frozen as: E(G) is partitioned into E_1 and E_2 such that (V(G), E_1) and (V(G), E_2) are both planar. The edge-disjoint reading loses nothing, because if two planar layers overlap then removing the shared edges from the second layer leaves a subgraph of a planar graph, which is planar, and does not change the union.

chi(G) >= 10 is frozen as: there is no proper vertex colouring of G with 9 colours. It does not require chi(G) = 10.

A witness must arrive as a canonical edge list with a content hash, one combinatorial planarity certificate per layer, and an exact certificate that no proper 9-colouring exists. A drawing, coordinates, or a planarity-library verdict without a replayable certificate is not accepted.

target_claim.statement: There exists a finite simple undirected graph G together with a partition of E(G) into sets E_1 and E_2 such that the spanning subgraphs (V(G), E_1) and (V(G), E_2) are both planar and there is no proper vertex colouring c : V(G) -> {1,...,9} with c(u) != c(v) for every edge uv in E(G).

assumption_claims.statement: G is a finite simple undirected graph: no loops, no multiple edges, finitely many vertices. G is biplanar iff E(G) can be partitioned into E_1 and E_2 such that the spanning subgraphs (V(G), E_1) and (V(G), E_2) on the same vertex set V(G) are both planar. Isolated vertices are permitted in either layer.
Every subgraph of a planar graph is planar. This is the standard textbook closure property of planarity under edge and vertex deletion.

The overlapping reading, in which E(G) = E_1 union E_2 with the layers allowed to share edges, defines the same class of graphs as the frozen partition reading. Given overlapping planar layers, replace E_2 by E_2 minus E_1: it is a subgraph of a planar graph and therefore planar by planar_subgraph_closure, and the union is unchanged. The edge-disjoint reading is frozen because it makes the certificate a partition, so the verifier can check that every edge of G is covered exactly once rather than at least once.

A layer is certified planar by a combinatorial embedding, not by a drawing: a rotation system giving, for every vertex, a cyclic order of its incident darts. The verifier traces faces using the next-dart permutation, checks that every dart is consumed exactly once, counts faces F per connected component, and checks Euler's formula V - E + F = 1 + c for the c components. A layer that fails is reported as not certified; a non-planarity claim about a layer would instead need an exhibited Kuratowski subdivision.

chi(G) >= 10 means exactly that no proper vertex colouring c : V(G) -> {1,...,9} exists, where proper means c(u) != c(v) for every edge uv. It does not assert chi(G) = 10, does not assert chi(G) <= any value, and is not weakened to a fractional, list, or local chromatic parameter.

The identity of a witness is the labelled graph: vertices are 0..n-1, every edge is an ordered pair (u, v) with u < v, the edge list is sorted lexicographically, the layer assignment is recorded per edge, and the content hash is sha256 over the canonically serialized bytes. This hash identifies a labelled graph and is not an isomorphism invariant; two isomorphic witnesses may hash differently and that is accepted, because the claim is about one exhibited graph.
A simple planar graph on n >= 3 vertices has at most 3n - 6 edges. This is the standard textbook consequence of Euler's formula.
A biplanar simple graph on n >= 3 vertices has at most 2 * (3n - 6) = 6n - 12 edges, because the two layers are edge-disjoint and each obeys planar_edge_bound.

K_11 is not biplanar: it has 55 edges while biplanar_edge_bound allows at most 6 * 11 - 12 = 54. Hence no complete graph on 11 or more vertices is biplanar, and the clique route to a chromatic lower bound cannot exceed 10. K_10 has 45 edges against the bound 48, so the edge count does not exclude it and its biplanarity is an open finite question for this slice.

For n >= 3, K_n is biplanar if and only if some spanning maximal planar graph T on n vertices, with exactly 3n - 6 edges, has planar complement in K_n. Given planar edge-disjoint layers of K_n, extend the first layer to a maximal planar spanning graph T using only edges already present in K_n; the complement of T is then contained in the second layer and is planar by planar_subgraph_closure. The converse direction is immediate.

Nothing on the trust path uses coordinates, geometry, or floating point. Planarity is decided combinatorially by rotation systems and integer face counts; colourability is decided by exact finite combinatorial search or by a checked UNSAT proof log. A picture, a force-directed layout, a numeric crossing count, and a spectral or relaxation bound on the chromatic number are exploration aids only and are never certificates.

Any exhaustive statement about 10-vertex triangulations depends on the generator covering every isomorphism class. Generating triangulations by vertex splitting from K_4 relies on a completeness theorem that is not acquired here, so its exhaustiveness is an open proof obligation and must be cross-checked against brute-force generation at smaller n before any exhaustion claim is recorded. Isomorph rejection is an optimization only: over-counting isomorphic copies is safe, omitting a class is not, so a canonical-form bug must fail towards duplication.

The planning notes report the current interval for the maximum chromatic number of a biplanar graph as 9 through 12, and thereby imply that a 9-chromatic biplanar graph is known. Both halves are untrusted, no source is acquired, and neither may be repeated as fact. Whether the biplanarity of K_10 is already settled in the literature is likewise unknown here; if it is settled, this slice is a reproduction and must be reported as one. The ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check must cover all three points.

The definition of biplanar used by the source that states the 9 through 12 interval is not acquired. Some authors define biplanar through thickness at most two, some through a union of two planar graphs, and some restrict to specific layer classes. The definition frozen here is authored locally; if the acquired source differs, the semantic alignment must be re-approved before any witness is reported against the source statement.

formalization.statement: exists G a finite simple graph, exists a partition E(G) = E_1 disjoint_union E_2, Planar(V(G), E_1) and Planar(V(G), E_2) and not exists c : V(G) -> {1,...,9} with (forall uv in E(G), c(u) != c(v))
quantifiers: exists G a finite simple undirected graph
exists a partition of E(G) into E_1 and E_2, both spanning subgraphs on V(G)
forall uv in E(G), the edge lies in exactly one of E_1 and E_2
not exists c : V(G) -> {1,...,9} proper on G, equivalently forall such c, exists an edge uv with c(u) = c(v)

quantifier_mapping: exists G a finite simple undirected graph
whose edge set is the union of two planar graphs
exists a partition of E(G) into E_1 and E_2 with both spanning layers planar
whose chromatic number is at least 10
not exists a proper colouring c : V(G) -> {1,...,9}
raise the lower bound from 9 to 10
no quantifier; this is an interpretation of the witness and is deliberately not part of the frozen target
definition_mapping: E(G) partitioned into two edge sets whose spanning subgraphs are both planar
a spanning subgraph admitting a rotation system whose traced faces satisfy V - E + F = 1 + c
no proper colouring with the 9 colours 1..9 exists
the sorted labelled edge list with per-edge layer assignment and its sha256 content hash
a rejected paraphrase; it coincides with the frozen definition only if the source means the same partition into planar spanning subgraphs
assumption_delta: Edge-disjointness is added to the source phrasing 'union of two planar graphs'; edge_disjointness_equivalence shows the class is unchanged, so the addition is a certificate convention rather than a strengthening.
Both layers are spanning subgraphs on the same vertex set, so a layer may contain isolated vertices; the planning statement does not say this.
Finiteness and simplicity are stated explicitly, because the planar edge bound and the colouring search both need them.
Nothing is assumed about the current known lower bound; the target is an absolute existence statement and does not reference 9.
edge_case_delta: A witness with chi(G) >= 11 also satisfies the frozen target; the target is a lower bound, not an equality.
n >= 10 is forced, because a graph on 9 or fewer vertices has a proper colouring with 9 colours.
A 10-clique inside G is by itself an exact certificate that no proper 9-colouring exists, and complete_graph_eleven_excluded shows this clique route caps at 10.
An empty second layer is admitted, so a planar graph would be biplanar; no planar graph can satisfy the colouring condition, so this edge case is consistent and harmless.
Adding an isolated vertex changes the canonical hash but neither planarity nor colourability, so witness identity is finer than the mathematical content.

success_criteria: an exhibited biplanar witness whose canonical hash, two rotation-system planarity certificates, and exact no-9-colouring certificate are all accepted by an independent verifier
a completed exhaustive decision of whether K_10 is biplanar, reported with its enumeration exhaustiveness obligation either discharged or explicitly open
a recorded closure of the clique route, namely that no complete graph can supply a witness beyond K_10, derived from the exact edge bound
or an explicit unresolved outcome that records the smallest remaining obligation together with the graph classes already excluded
stopping_rules: stop on an exact witness whose planarity and non-9-colourability certificates are both independently replayed
stop when the frozen enumeration envelope for 10-vertex maximal planar graphs is exhausted, recording the bounded outcome and nothing stronger
stop when the fresh model spend reaches USD 20
stop when no new certified layer, no new excluded class, and no new refuted route have been produced across two consecutive review points
never promote a completed bounded enumeration into a claim that no biplanar graph has chromatic number at least 10, nor into a claim about the general chromatic bound
